sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the area between central and southern Calabria (near the city of Catanzaro), flanked by the southern shoulder of the Sila massif and the Lamezia-Catanzaro fault (to the north) and the Serre Mts. and the Capo Vaticano promontory (to the south). This source is a near-vertical, S-dipping, left-lateral strike-slip fault, part of the strike-slip system that dissects and advances the central and southern Calabrian arc toward SE.
Historical catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a remarkable concentration of damaging earthquakes in the the area. In particular, this region has been struck, from north to south, by the: 27 March 1638 (Mw 7.0, Calabria), 28 March 1783 (Mw 6.9, Calabria), 4 April 1626 (Mw 6.1, Girifalco), 1 March 1783 (Mw 5.9, Calabria Centrale), and 8 September 1905 (Mw 7.1, Calabria) events.
This region marks the passage between the Apulian-Appenninic sector of Calabria (to the north) and the Calabrian Arc (to the south), as shown by the difference in terrain, paleogeography, abrupt shift in strike of the belt (from ca. N-S in the Sila massif to NE-SW in the Serre Mts.), and landscape features. Unsurprisingly, such a "hinge zone" poses several difficulties concerning its active tectonics and, of course, the issues of earthquake faulting are of primary relevance â€“ all of this enhanced by the elusive Calabrian geology.
So far, investigators have concentrated on the structural geology of the region and the present-day role of the "Catanzaro Straits" remains unclear. Based on the regional geological setup and information from subsurface data, we believe that this region is controlled by the south-easterly advancement of the Calabrian Arc toward the Ionian Sea. We also propose that this source includes the fault segment that has caused the 28 March 1783 earthquake.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the mapped regional structures. Also the dip was based on geological and geometrical considerations. Rake is indicative of normal to left-lateral strike-slip faulting, based on regional geological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and geometrical considerations. Slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.
